These represent a formally recognized area of study within a program. They:
Are coded in eCampus
Have defined requirements that students must complete
Appear on the student’s transcript
Are formally created and maintained through the Specializations section of Kuali
Note: The terminology used may vary by system or University Manual terminology. For curricular proposal purposes, these structures are treated as specializations in Kuali.

These represent an optional area of study within a program. They:
Are not coded in eCampus
May include suggested courses or course sequences to guide students
Do not appear on the student’s transcript
Are described within the program description to which they belong
Do not require a separate curricular proposal

Both Accelerated Bachelor’s to Master’s (ABM) programs and “4 + 1” programs are formally recognized Specializations, but they differ in how they are structured and which degree program they belong to.
ABM Specializations
Are inherited by the Master’s degree
Identify a defined pathway from the Bachelor’s degree into the Master’s degree
Include an identified set of courses that may be double-counted toward both the Bachelor’s and Master’s degree requirements
“4 + 1” Specializations
Are inherited by the Bachelor’s degree
Do not include courses that are double-counted toward both degrees
Provide guidance on courses students should take during the final semesters of their undergraduate degree to help shorten the time needed to complete the Master’s degree

Requisites
Tags: courses
Short Description: Courses or other requirements that must be completed before or at the time of enrollment in a course. Requisites may include prerequisites and corequisites.
Requisites
Requisites are courses, conditions, or other requirements that determine whether a student is eligible to enroll in a course. Requisites may be required before enrollment, at the time of enrollment, or may establish other conditions for registration.
Common types of requisites include:
Prerequisites: Courses or requirements that must be completed before enrolling in the course.
Corequisites: Courses or requirements that must be completed concurrently with the course.
Other enrollment requirements: Additional conditions that may apply to enrollment, such as minimum class standing, program or major restrictions, or other eligibility requirements.
When entering requisites in Kuali, ensure that the requirements accurately reflect the conditions under which students should be permitted to enroll.

Understand the Workflow
Understand the Workflow

The curriculum approval process generally follows the sequence shown in the URI Curricular Approval Process Flowchart. Specific steps may vary by college, department, proposal type, and whether the proposal requires additional levels of review.
URI Curricular Approval Process Flowchart

Proposal Development Faculty use the forms in Kuali Curriculum Management to develop the proposal and work with other stakeholders as appropriate.
Department Review The proposal is reviewed through the appropriate departmental process.
College Curriculum Committee Review The College Curriculum Committee reviews the proposal.
College Dean Approval The College Dean approves the proposal for Faculty Senate review.
Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee Review The Curriculum & Standards Committee, the General Education Committee, or the Graduate Council reviews the proposal.
Faculty Senate Approval The Faculty Senate considers the curriculum committee's recommendation and votes.
University President Approval Any curricular item that is not a course must be reviewed and approved by the University President.
URI Board of Trustees Approval In addition to the University President’s approval, new Majors and Degrees are also reviewed by the Board of Trustees.

While all Colleges follow the curriculum approval process established in the University Manual, each College may have its own internal approval process based on its departmental and governance structures. To download a flowchart of a specific College’s approval process, select the College below.

Bachelor Degree Requirements

Complete of a minimum of 120 credits (some majors require more)

Complete the coursework and other requirements for the curriculum of the major with the minimum grades per course and overall grade point averages for that major, or portions of that major, as specified in the section of the catalog which describes the requirements for each major
Complete General Education requirements, as specified elsewhere in this catalog
Abide by community standards as defined in the University Manual and Student Handbook
Complete the senior year in residence at URI
Earn one half of the total number of credits needed in the major at URI (same for a minor, if one is being pursued)
Transfer no more than half of the credits required for graduation from a two-year institution
Earn at least one-fourth of the credits required for graduation in-residence at URI (usually at least 30 credits)*
Students should review all major/degree requirements with their academic advisor to ensure completion of all course, credit and GPA minimums.

Topics Course
Tags: courses
Short Description: A course that allows different topics to be offered under the same course number.
Topics Course
Topics courses allow different topics to be offered under the same course number.
8.81.20 Open-ended Course. An Open-ended Course shall be administered by the department which originated it. Initially, an open-ended course shall be proposed and approved in the same manner as other permanent courses (8.81.10). Prior to offering a specific topic the content of the course shall be approved in a department meeting.
8.81.21 After approval of each offering of an open-ended course topic, a copy of the title, subtitle, and description shall be forwarded for schedule authorization to the Office of Enrollment Services via the dean of the college in which the department resides. The dean’s authorization shall ensure that no overlap exists between specific topics and existing courses.

8.81.22 A specific topic within an open-ended course may be offered three times. After three offerings the topic shall be approved through the appropriate channels as either a permanent course or as a permanent topic within an open-ended course and shall be included in the University Catalog.
